newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir not to raise island dispute with Suharto.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir not to raise island dispute with Suharto.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday he will not raise the issue of the dispute over a group of islands with Indonesian President Suharto, who arrives on Sunday for a two-day visit.
"That (territorial dispute) matter has been decided," the national Bernama news agency quoted Suharto as telling reporters after opening the Gerakan party's national convention.

Indonesia's official Antara news agency reported on September 22 that President Suharto was visiting Malaysia to resolve the dispute over the Sipadan and Ligitan islands, located off the coast of Borneo and claimed by both countries.
Mahathir said his meeting with Suharto would focus on bilateral ties and their stand on the Association of South East Nations (ASEAN) and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).
Kuala Lumpur has suggested taking the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague.
But Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who will accompany Suharto on the trip, was quoted as saying that Jakarta would agree to the suggestion only if bilateral talks on the matter failed.
Malaysia is also involved in a dispute over the South China Sea's Spratly Islands with Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei, China and Taiwan.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Mahathir last met Suharto in Bogor, Indonesia at the APEC summit in November 1994. The Indonesian President's last visit to Malaysia was in 1993.
